claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets are primarily governed by variations in local chemical ordering.
Local chemical ordering modulates the distribution of local stacking-fault energies.
The stacking-fault-energy landscape controls the balance between dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
The stacking-fault-energy landscape can control stress-induced phase transformation in some alloys in this family.
The selected alloys can be produced as single-phase FCC materials by thermomechanical processing.
Selected quaternary and ternary variants differ from equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni by removal of one or two constituent elements.
Applying identical thermomechanical processing across the compositions provides a controlled comparison of composition-dependent deformation behavior.
Dislocation motion, deformation twinning, and possible FCC-to-HCP transformation are active at room temperature or moderately elevated temperatures in the investigated alloys.
Enhanced local chemical order reduces effective stacking-fault energy in localized regions.
Localized reductions in stacking-fault energy facilitate deformation twinning.
Localized reductions in stacking-fault energy can facilitate transformation-induced plasticity.
Twinning and transformation-induced plasticity redistribute strain and sustain work hardening.
Twinning or transformation-induced plasticity can increase ductility without compromising strength.
Diminished local chemical order produces a higher average stacking-fault energy.
Higher stacking-fault energy makes dislocation slip the dominant deformation mechanism.
Dislocation-dominated variants will have higher yield strength but lower ductility.
Relative to equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, variants with greater local chemical order will exhibit more deformation twinning and possibly more FCC-to-HCP transformation.
Relative to equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, variants with greater local chemical order will exhibit enhanced ductility and more balanced work hardening.
Relative to equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, variants with lower local chemical order will exhibit higher yield strength and reduced ductility.
The proposed relationship may not apply when significant secondary phases are present or compositions differ markedly from the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni family.
